summary: This bill requires the Small Business Administration to ensure its own rulemakings impose no net cost on small businesses starting in fiscal year 2026 and mandates annual congressional reports on other federal agencies' regulatory costs to small businesses.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires the SBA to ensure its small business regulatory budget (compliance costs to small businesses from SBA rules) is not greater than zero, meaning net new regulatory costs cannot increase. It also mandates no additional funds for the Act itself. However, this addresses private sector compliance costs from regulations, not federal government expenditures or budget allocations. There is no provision to expand or reduce government spending directly. No bearing on government spending.

The bill text makes no mention of taxes, tax rates, deductions, or any tax policy. It focuses solely on regulatory compliance costs from SBA rulemakings, which are distinct from taxation. No relation.
No references to healthcare, insurance, providers, or related policies. The bill is exclusively about SBA regulatory costs on small businesses in general. No bearing.
The bill does not address firearms, Second Amendment, or gun regulations. Unrelated.
No content on immigration, borders, visas, or protections. Focused on SBA rules for small businesses. No relation.
No mention of abortion, reproductive rights, or related issues. Irrelevant.
No provisions affecting military spending, defense budget, or armed forces. SBA-related only. No bearing.

While the bill deals with regulatory costs, SBA rulemakings (e.g., size standards, loans) do not primarily involve environmental protections or climate rules, which are handled by agencies like EPA. No specific engagement with environmental topics.
No discussion of welfare, food stamps, unemployment, or safety net programs. Unrelated to SBA regulatory costs.
No references to schools, funding, choice, or education policy. No relation.
No content on drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement. Irrelevant.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, reform, or justice system issues. No bearing.
No mention of trade, tariffs, free trade, or protectionism. SBA rules are domestic small business administration. Unrelated.

While no additional funds are authorized, the bill neither increases nor decreases federal debt or prioritizes reduction. Regulatory compliance savings to businesses do not directly impact national debt. No genuine engagement.
No provisions on LGBTQ+ protections or limitations. Unrelated.
No reference to foreign aid or international assistance. Domestic SBA focus only. No relation.
No content on voting access, elections, or integrity measures. Irrelevant.

SBA rules might tangentially affect small tech firms (e.g., size standards), and reducing regulatory costs implies less oversight, but the bill does not specifically engage tech, data, or privacy issues. Not genuinely about this topic.

SBA rulemakings occasionally touch employee-related definitions (e.g., for size standards), but the bill is not about labor protections, unions, or employer flexibility specifically. No direct or clear relation to labor/union policy.
No mention of religious exemptions, discrimination, or civil rights. Unrelated.
